scenario_name: CrewAI-style Content Production Crew — Case 2 for AgentCoordKG
description: Hand-authored scenario following CrewAI's real Agent/Task/Process/allow_delegation schema (confirmed via official CrewAI documentation), NOT a live CrewAI run. Demonstrates AgentCoordKG's coverage of a real framework's native coordination schema, and surfaces a key symmetric finding: CrewAI's Process (sequential task ordering) and allow_delegation mechanisms -- which HarnessKG's Existing-KG Decision Tree explicitly judged out of scope, belonging to AgentCoordKG -- map DIRECTLY onto AgentCoordKG's dependsOn and delegatesTask relations, confirming the intended division of labor between the two companion ontologies.

_crewai_native_log._comment: Mimics a real CrewAI crew configuration using CrewAI's actual concepts (Agent role/goal/backstory, Task.context chaining, Process=sequential, allow_delegation). Not itself part of the RDF instance data.

tasks.description: Write draft article on topic X

_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Agent (role, goal, backstory): Maps directly to ak:Agent, with 'role' captured via hasRole -- no ontology change needed.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Task (description, expected_output): Maps directly to ak:Task -- no ontology change needed.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Process=sequential (task ordering): SYMMETRIC FINDING: maps directly to dependsOn (Task -> Task). HarnessKG's Existing-KG Decision Tree explicitly judged CrewAI's Process as out-of-scope, belonging to AgentCoordKG's Task.dependsOn territory -- this scenario confirms that judgment by showing Process maps cleanly here.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.allow_delegation (agent hands a task to: SYMMETRIC FINDING: maps directly to delegatesTask (Agent -> Task). HarnessKG's Decision Tree likewise flagged CrewAI's Delegation as AgentCoordKG territory -- confirmed here as a direct, clean match.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Task.tools (e.g. web_search): Maps directly to Task.usesTool (datatype property) -- no ontology change needed.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Task.context (prior task output referenc: Interpreted (not native to CrewAI) as an implicit Message-passing mechanism -- CrewAI has no explicit Message primitive; task-to-task context chaining is our semantic interpretation, disclosed as such.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Crew-level memory=True (cross-task memor: NO AgentCoordKG equivalent -- AgentCoordKG has no Memory or Harness-like coordinating-container class; this functionality belongs entirely to the companion HarnessKG ontology (where Crew's memory role would map to Harness+coordinatesMemory). This is the clean counterpart to the Process/Delegation findings above: CrewAI's coordination-flavored features map to AgentCoordKG, while its memory-flavored features map to HarnessKG -- confirming a clean division of labor discovered from the framework's own native schema, not asserted a priori.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Delegation under role/capacity mismatch: Interpreted (not native to CrewAI) as violatesConstraint -> Conflict, consistent with the same interpretive treatment used in the illustrative AgentCoordKG scenario.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Acceptance of the Senior Editor's final: Interpreted (not native to CrewAI) as triggering ak:Decision -- same treatment as the task-output-acceptance Decisions found in HarnessKG's AutoGen/CrewAI/LangGraph/MetaGPT scenarios.

story_summary: A CrewAI Content Writer is delegated an article to draft, but the task is initially assigned to an editor whose role doesn't match -- a role-mismatch conflict. The article is then routed to the Senior Editor, who reviews and approves it.
